entities.summary: Francesco di Tommaso Soderini was a major diplomatic and Church figure of Renaissance Italy, and brother of Piero Soderini. He was an adversary of the Medici family. Born in 1440s in Florence, Italy, Soderini rose to prominence as a leader of the Florentine Republic. He served as the First Secretary of State and later as the Chancellor of the Republic, playing a crucial role in shaping the city-state's politics. Soderini's diplomatic efforts aimed to maintain the Republic's independence and resist the growing power of the Medici family. He was a key figure in the 1469–1470 Pazzi conspiracy against the Medici, which ultimately failed. Soderini's legacy extends to the 1520s, when he was a prominent figure in the Italian Renaissance humanist movement. He was a patron of the arts and a supporter of the works of the poet and statesman, Lorenzo de' Medici. Soderini's death in 1524 marked the end of an era for Florence, as the city began to transition from a republic to a duchy under the rule of the Medici family.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Francesco di Tommaso Soderini played a significant role in shaping the politics of Renaissance Italy, particularly in Florence. His diplomatic efforts and brotherhood with Piero Soderini contributed to the city-state's independence and influence. However, the Medici family's eventual rise to power marked the end of the Florentine Republic.
